question: Where can I get the environmental assessment decisions on energy projects in Spain, with project, developer, location, date and outcome?

answer.summary: No complete structured Spanish inventory was found. The BOE publishes state decisions. Castilla y León has an index of 5,388 ordinary EIA files (797 energy), with publication dates and no promoter or outcome. Andalucía lists granted unified authorizations. An unofficial UAM compilation of BOE records for PV and hybrid projects covers 2014–2025 (570 rows, 470 labelled favorable and 100 unfavorable). Official coverage and the latest available decisions remain unverified.
main_caveats: Environmental decisions are distinct from final construction or operating authorization.
The UAM compilation is non-official. Its description says favorable DIAs only, but 100 of its 570 rows are unfavorable; it covers PV and hybrid projects, not all energy.
The BOE API has no DIA keyword search. A full enumeration needs a day-by-day scan of the summaries, which was not run; only 2025-12-29 and 2014-11-19 were checked.
Castilla y León declares an annual update for its case index. Its BOCYL field is a publication date and its rows have no promoter or outcome.
Andalucía lists granted authorizations only, so it cannot establish the number of adverse decisions. Its first-page dates are from 2009.
BOE and SABIA are not verified as complete inventories of regional decisions, and regional gazettes outside Castilla y León and Andalucía were not searched in this pass.
answer.confidence_reason: Re-tested the BOE route, the Castilla y León index and the Andalucía list, and cross-checked the non-official compilation against two BOE texts. National completeness and most regional gazettes remain unverified.

attributes.note: CyL project names (797 energy rows); UAM project names (570 PV and hybrid rows); AAU installation names (mixed sectors); BOE resolution titles.
attributes.gap_note: Names are not a shared identifier across sources. Regional gazettes and other autonomous communities were not checked.

attributes.note: UAM 'Promotor DIA' in 569 of 570 rows; BOE texts name the promoter; AAU list has an 'Empresa' column; CyL gives no developer.
attributes.gap_note: The Ferreira II BOE text names no promoter. The UAM 'Promotor real' column is not verified against the BOE.

attributes.note: Municipality and province in BOE texts, UAM (570 rows) and CyL (797 energy rows); AAU has Municipio; no coordinates in any source.
attributes.gap_note: Municipality precision only. Completeness across autonomous communities is not verified.

attributes.note: BOE resolution date. Two UAM rows match the resolution date under 'Fecha publicación DIA'. CyL supplies BOCYL publication dates.
attributes.gap_note: Publication dates in the regional index do not establish decision dates. Check individual resolutions and distinguish both dates in new samples.

attributes.note: UAM 'Estado': 470 Favorable and 100 Desfavorable (two BOE texts checked). BOE text states 'desfavorable' explicitly. AAU lists granted authorizations only.
attributes.gap_note: Favorable decisions carry conditions that the UAM table does not show. Adverse decisions outside the UAM table are unknown.

attributes.note: UAM ends in 2025 (resolution 2025-12-17, BOE publication 2025-12-29). Latest BOCYL publication in the checked CyL export: 2025-12-17.
attributes.gap_note: Two BOE dates were sampled. The latest decision in the official national or regional collections remains unchecked.

attributes.note: CyL 1989–2025 (all types; energy from 1996). UAM 2014–2025 (570 rows; 2022 and 2023 hold 456). BOE summaries checked on two dates only.
attributes.gap_note: Gaps: UAM has 26 rows for 2014–2021. BOE history before 2014 and comparability across sources are not verified.

attributes.note: The Castilla y León ordinary-EIA case index declares an annual update. This is the index schedule.
attributes.gap_note: The update cadence of UAM and comprehensive decision collections has not been established. Daily BOE summaries do not imply daily environmental decisions.
